podcast.title: Homophobic Hate Crime and Confession
podcast.body: Both men confessed to carrying out a homophobic hate crime after a night of drinking, during which they actively sought someone to attack. They were subsequently tried, jailed, and released after serving seven years in prison. "Both men confessed to a homophobic hate crime that they carried out after going drinking and then looking for someone to attack."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock

podcast.title: Kielers Park Murder Involvement
podcast.body: Vocalist John Nödtveidt was implicated in the "Kielers Park Murder," a notorious criminal case in Guttenberg, Sweden, involving the shooting death of Joseph Ben Medoure, a gay Algerian man. "John Noddvite was the vocalist for an extreme metal band from Sweden called Dissection."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock

podcast.title: Murder and Ritual Suicide
podcast.body: John Nödtveidt, associated with the band Dissection, murdered a gay man from Algeria and subsequently served time in jail for the crime. After his release from prison, Nödtveidt committed ritual suicide. "John Notvelt was with a band called Dissection. He murdered a gay man from Algeria and was sent to jail. And when he got out, he committed ritual suicide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Satanic Cult Membership
podcast.body: Nödtveidt and his accomplice, Vlad (from another metal band), were both members of a satanic cult called Tempolo Black Light. "Both of them were members of a satanic cult called Tempolo Black Light."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock

podcast.title: Suicide (Two Years After Release)
podcast.body: Two years after his release from prison, Nödtveidt died by suicide. His body was discovered arranged in a ring of candles, with a book of satanic rituals found beside him. "Two years later, Nonvite was dead by his own hand."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock

xref.title: Post-Tour Financial Issues and Death (1994-2022)
xref.body: After the tumultuous 90s, Andy Fletcher managed to regain stability and continue as a functioning member of Depeche Mode, despite facing financial issues from bad investments, which he also survived. Sadly, he died at his home on May 26, 2022, at the age of 60, from an aortic dissection, a sudden and massive internal bleeding event. "But then Fletcher died of an aortic dissection in his home on May 26, 2022."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Lux Interior's Death (February 4, 2009)
xref.body: Lux interior died suddenly on February 4, 2009, from an aortic dissection, an undiagnosed condition where the body's largest artery ruptures, leading to rapid internal bleeding. He and Poison Ivy had been married for 37 years. "But then on February 4th, 2009, Lux suddenly died after suffering an aortic dissection, an undiagnosed condition where your aorta, the largest artery in your body, bursts, and you bleed out internally in seconds."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Andy Fletcher's Cause of Death (2022)
xref.body: Andy Fletcher of Depeche Mode died in 2022 from an aortic dissection, the same undiagnosed condition that caused the death of Lux Interior of The Cramps. "This is the same thing that killed Andy Fletcher of Depeche Mode in 2022."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Andy Fletcher's Sudden Death and Cause
xref.body: Andy Fletcher died suddenly at his home on May 26, 2022, from an aortic dissection, a condition where the inner layer of the largest artery in the body tears, allowing blood to leak out and potentially rupture completely, leading to immediate death. "Andy died suddenly at his home on May 26, 2022, of something called an aortic dissection."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Aortic Dissection Shared by Other Artists
xref.body: Andy Fletcher's cause of death, an aortic dissection, is the same condition that also claimed the lives of actors John Ritter and Alan Thicke, as well as musicians Lux Interior of The Cramps and Peter Steele of Type O Negative. "This is the same thing that killed actors John Ritter and Alan Thick. And it also killed Lux interior singer for the cramps and Peter Steele of the bad typo negative."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Cause of Death: Aortic Dissection
xref.body: Andy Fletcher's cause of death was an aortic dissection, a rare condition that is seldom diagnosed in advance due to few warning signs and can result from factors like high blood pressure or congenital conditions, leading to rapid internal bleeding. "Cause of death was an aortic dissection, a rare condition that's almost never diagnosed in advance because there's no real reason to look for it because there are a few, if any, warning signs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: In Memoriam of Those Lost in 2022

xref.title: Detection Challenges for Aortic Dissection
xref.body: Detecting the risk of an aortic dissection typically requires advanced imaging such as a CT scan, MRI, or ultrasound, as there is no other way to tell if one is in danger. "but unless you have a CT scan or an MRI or an ultrasound, there's no way to tell if you're in danger."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rarity of Aortic Dissection
xref.body: Aortic dissection is a rare condition, affecting approximately three out of every 100,000 people annually, with men being more susceptible than women, and the average age for such an event being 63. Andy Fletcher was 60 when he died. "Only about three and a hundred thousand people are hit with such a thing every year."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Risk Factors for Aortic Dissection
xref.body: An aortic dissection can be caused by a genetic condition, high blood pressure, and is not helped by smoking and cocaine use. "Could have been a genetic condition could have been due to high blood pressure, smoking and cocaine don't help."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
